conviction_note: Four findings net to -3.5: the two revenue-side mechanics (a quarter run on $1.6m of cash plus a never-press-released $10m revolver, and the first quarter with FEI-Elcom fully removed) argue the stale 2026-07-16 consensus of $17.85m/$0.15 is set above what the quarter could physically produce, partly offset by a record funded-backlog print, and lightly dinged by a board-affiliated 11% holder whose 60-day lock-up lifts twelve sessions after the call; the number is deliberately well inside the 14.4% implied move because the distribution here is genuinely two-tailed.

findings.finding: FEIM entered the quarter with $1.6m of cash (down from $4.5m a year earlier) and had no committed liquidity until it quietly signed its first-ever secured revolver — only $10m, pledging substantially all assets of FEI and FEI-Zyfer, with covenant testing beginning 2026-07-31 — on 12 June, six weeks into a quarter for which the only published consensus asks $17.85m of revenue, i.e. the highest quarterly revenue in six quarters and +29% YoY, in a long-lead-material atomic-clock business; the $73m of equity proceeds did not land until 30 July, one day before quarter end.
findings.why_not_priced: The revolver 8-K was never press-released — StockTitan's FEIM feed from June to September 2026 lists no June item at all, going straight from 27 May to 15 July — so a debt-free-for-decades company pledging all its assets for $10m mid-quarter never reached the wire. If the market had connected it to Q1 capacity, the 25-delta skew would not be sitting at +1.16 (essentially balanced) and the stock would not be up 7.7% in the five sessions into the print; instead the tape is treating the 20-day drawdown as pure post-offering supply.
findings.independence: Independent confirmation of the $1.6m starting cash position and of the working-capital use of proceeds comes from two other documents: the Q4 FY2026 8-K release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/39020/000118518526002982/feimex99-1.htm, 2026-07-15) and the prospectus supplement's use-of-proceeds language 'capital expenditures, working capital and other general corporate purposes' (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/39020/000118518526003167/feim424b5072826.htm, 2026-07-28). The $17.85m/$0.15 bar itself is from a different source (https://www.marketbeat.com/earnings/reports/2026-9-10-frequency-electronics-inc-stock/).

findings.finding: This is the first quarter with zero FEI-Elcom revenue — the 10-K states FEI-Elcom designed and manufactured RF microwave modules 'until April 30, 2026' and was converted to an LLC and restructured effective that date — while the Q1 FY2026 comparison base of $13.8m still contained it; management quantified roughly $1m of revenue forgone in Q4 FY2026 alone from the decision and said the winddown continues through fiscal 2027, so consensus $17.85m implies closer to +38% growth on the continuing base rather than the headline +29%.
findings.why_not_priced: The restructuring is discussed publicly only as a margin story (the $3.8m inventory write-down that took reported Q4 gross margin to 1.0%); no coverage subtracts the lost revenue line from the FY2027 comparison. If it had been priced, the two published FY2027 revenue estimates would not both be dated 2026-07-16 and unchanged since, and the sell-side commentary would frame FY2027 growth ex-Elcom rather than off the $63.2m reported base.
findings.independence: The ~$1m of Q4 revenue forgone and the through-FY2027 winddown come from the Q4 FY2026 call, a different document (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/07/23/frequency-electronics-feim-q4-2026-earnings-call-transcript/, 2026-07-23). Note this finding shares a direction, but not a document, with finding 1 — both bear on Q1 revenue, so a scorer should not treat their sizes as fully additive.

findings.finding: FEIM press-released $26m of new awards inside the quarter — $18m on 23 July (including an $11m first-time proliferated-satellite win) and $8m on 27 July for lunar PNT atomic clocks — against roughly $16-17m of likely revenue, so funded backlog should print at a new record near $120-125m (and higher if the $16m announced 27 May was booked after 30 April), versus $111m at 30 April and $71m at 31 July 2025; FEIM's two largest positive reactions in the baseline, +30.57% and +28.81%, were both record-backlog prints.
findings.why_not_priced: The awards themselves are wire copy; what is not published anywhere is the roll-forward into a backlog number, and backlog is the single disclosure this stock has historically repriced on. With only two analysts covering and both estimates frozen at 2026-07-16, there is no published backlog forecast for anyone to trade against. If it were priced, the stock would not be 20.4% below its 52-week high going into a print that is very likely to carry a record backlog headline.
findings.independence: Confirmed by a separate release and a separate outlet: the $18m award (https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/07/23/3332036/7746/en/Frequency-Electronics-Inc-Announces-Contract-Awards-Valued-at-Approximately-18-million.html, 2026-07-23) and the 10-K's statement that approximately 73% of the $111m backlog is expected to be filled in FY2027 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/39020/000118518526002997/feim10k043026.htm). Cuts against findings 1 and 2 in direction, which is why the net number is only -3.5.

findings.finding: Edenbrook Capital — whose founder Jonathan Brolin sits on FEIM's board and stands for re-election on 7 October — sold 652,174 shares at $57.50 into the July offering and took only a 60-day lock-up dated from the 28 July underwriting agreement, so the lock-up lifts around 26-28 September, twelve sessions after this print, while Brolin still beneficially owns 1,242,941 shares, about 11.1% of the 11.2m shares now outstanding and roughly six days of the 208k average daily volume.
findings.why_not_priced: The 60-day term appears only in Item 4 of Schedule 13D/A Amendment No. 12, filed as a raw primary_doc.xml with no press release and no 8-K; the aggregators reduced this to a single 'insiders sold $37.5m' line with no expiry date attached. Had the market focused on it, the put/call open interest ratio would not be 0.76 with only 537 contracts of total open interest, and the September 18 chain would show a bid for downside past the print rather than a 79%-of-mid ATM spread.
findings.independence: The share count the 11.1% is measured against is corroborated independently by the 424B5's post-offering share table of 10,955,824 plus the 260,869-share greenshoe exercised in the 5 August 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/39020/000118518526003285/feim8k080526.htm, 2026-08-05). Brolin's board seat and 7 October re-election come from the proxy (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/39020/000118518526003746/feimdef14a082526.htm, 2026-08-28).

searched_and_found_nothing: FPDS/USASpending direct federal award history — FEIM sells almost entirely as a subcontractor to primes, so the only direct records since May 2026 are two ~$314k Army SBIR magnetometer mods and a $500 placeholder delivery order; no signal
MDA SHIELD / Golden Dome — FEIM holds an IDIQ seat but MDA has awarded 2,440 companies seats, so the seat carries no information

SDA Tranche 3 / MILNET disruption to LEO clock demand — the Space Force's shift away from the SDA transport layer was reported in April 2026, before FEIM's last print, so it is not new information into this one
FEIM careers page — routes to LinkedIn/Indeed with no enumerated postings, so no headcount-trend read was obtainable
424B5 prospectus supplement 'Recent Developments' — there is none; no preliminary Q1 figures, no updated backlog date, no acquisition language
Form 4 activity since the offering — only one, a routine 9,022-share tax-withholding disposal by CFO Bernstein on 2026-07-31; no open-market insider buying after the 19% drawdown
DEF 14A of 2026-08-28 — no share authorisation increase, no new equity plan, no new director nominee, no auditor change
A published sell-side estimate revision after the 28 July offering — none found; both covering analysts' numbers are still dated 2026-07-16
A specific news catalyst for the 12-21 August slide from $78.34 to $61.69 — no company-specific item found in that window
baseline_tension: It cuts against the 5-day run-up of +7.7% into the print and is only weakly supported by the +1.16 skew, which is close enough to balanced that the option market is making no directional statement; the 20-day -18.8% is explained by the July equity offering and the August momentum unwind rather than by earnings fear, so the drawdown is not already discounting the Q1 revenue mechanics described here.
